domain: team dinner at an Indian restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant recommendation and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a group dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're planning a team dinner this Saturday at an Indian restaurant. Got any tips on what to order for a group?

flow_info.value: Five of us: me, Priya, Sam, Derek, and Noor
Sam ate peanut satay at a Thai place last year and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Derek was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
Budget is around 30-35 dollars per person
Derek just told me he has to leave by 7:30 to catch a flight, but he asked if we could pack him some food to take to the airport
Noor told me her doctor cleared her — the kidney thing is fully resolved, no more low-sodium diet
Noor wants to bring her husband Arjun along
Dishes to check: chicken tikka masala, paneer butter masala, lamb rogan josh, garlic naan, shrimp biryani, gulab jamun

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw or undercooked food, should avoid high-mercury fish
inference_chain: Pregnancy → avoid raw/undercooked food, high-mercury fish

constraints.value: Cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Sam ate peanut satay at a Thai place last year and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Throat swelling + EpiPen after peanut satay → severe peanut allergy
Peanut allergy → must avoid peanuts and peanut-derived ingredients

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products made from them
constraints.surface_form: Derek was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
No wheat → naan, roti, samosa, most breads are off-limits

constraints.surface_form: Noor has been dealing with some kidney issues, her doctor put her on a pretty strict diet

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes)
constraints.surface_form: Arjun's family is Jain, he's pretty observant about it
inference_chain: Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes)

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a team dinner at an Indian restaurant for Saturday. You will introduce 5 people with various dietary issues in a burst, then updates will come in: Derek leaves early but wants takeaway, Noor's kidney restriction gets lifted, Noor's husband Arjun joins (he's Jain). At the end you will share a list of 6 dishes and ask if there are any issues. You must NEVER hint at what the problems are — just list the dishes and ask.

You are a calm, cooperative team organizer. You always refer to your colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'Priya told me...', 'Sam mentioned...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for colleague updates

aims.success_criteria: Agent checks each of the 6 dishes against all active constraints and identifies problems per item
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 dishes against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Chicken tikka masala: problematic for Arjun (Jain — no meat). Paneer butter masala: problematic for Arjun (typically contains garlic and onion — Jain diet excludes root vegetables including garlic and onion). Lamb rogan josh: problematic for Arjun (Jain — no meat), and contains garlic/onion. Garlic naan: problematic for Arjun (contains garlic — Jain restriction on root vegetables; also contains wheat/gluten) and must not be packed for Derek's takeaway (celiac — naan is wheat-based). Shrimp biryani: problematic for Arjun (Jain — no meat/fish/seafood). Gulab jamun: fine for everyone currently dining in. Note: Noor has no dietary restrictions anymore (kidney issue resolved). Derek is leaving early but wants takeaway — his celiac constraint applies only to what gets packed for him.
required_elements: Chicken tikka masala is problematic for Arjun because he is Jain and cannot eat meat
Paneer butter masala is problematic for Arjun because it typically contains garlic and onion, which are root vegetables excluded under Jain dietary practice
Lamb rogan josh is problematic for Arjun because he is Jain and cannot eat meat
Garlic naan is problematic for Arjun because garlic is a root vegetable excluded under Jain dietary practice
Garlic naan must not be packed for Derek's takeaway because naan is wheat-based and Derek has celiac disease — cannot eat gluten
Shrimp biryani is problematic for Arjun because Jain diet excludes seafood and fish
Gulab jamun is fine for everyone currently attending
Noor has no dietary restrictions anymore — agent treats her as able to eat anything
forbidden_elements: Flagging any dish as problematic for Noor due to sodium or kidney diet (her restriction was removed)
Saying Derek cannot eat at the restaurant at all (he is leaving early but wants takeaway packed)
Flagging garlic naan as problematic for Derek at the table (he is leaving early; the gluten issue only matters for his packed takeaway)
Saying Sam has a general nut allergy or tree nut allergy (he specifically has a peanut allergy)
Flagging dishes as unsafe for Sam without evidence they contain peanuts (Indian cuisine does not typically use peanuts in tikka masala, rogan josh, naan, biryani, or gulab jamun)
Saying Arjun cannot eat dairy or paneer (Jain diet allows dairy; the issue with paneer butter masala is the garlic and onion, not the paneer itself)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns at an Indian restaurant. The agent must track: (1) Priya is 7 months pregnant → avoid raw/undercooked food and high-mercury fish (none of the probe dishes trigger this — all are cooked, no high-mercury fish), (2) Sam has a severe peanut allergy inferred from the EpiPen incident (peanuts are not a standard ingredient in the probe dishes, so Sam should be fine), (3) Derek has celiac disease → no gluten/wheat (he leaves early but wants takeaway — his constraint applies to packed food only, specifically garlic naan cannot be packed for him), (4) Noor's kidney/low-sodium restriction is REMOVED mid-conversation (doctor cleared her), (5) Arjun joins late as Noor's husband and is Jain → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables including onion and garlic (this is the highest-constraint entity, affecting chicken tikka masala, paneer butter masala, lamb rogan josh, garlic naan, and shrimp biryani). The key traps: paneer butter masala LOOKS vegetarian-friendly but contains garlic and onion (Jain restriction on root vegetables); garlic naan has a scope distinction (problematic for Arjun at the table AND cannot be packed for Derek's takeaway due to gluten); gulab jamun is the clearly-fine item; Sam's peanut allergy should NOT be over-generalized to flag dishes without peanuts; Noor's removed constraint should not ghost into the evaluation.

mechanism: Entity EXIT with scope change: person leaves but wants something packed/saved
